summary: Disclosed remote-agent runner routes WebRTC datachannel commands into local shell/PTY
details: The package is a daemon whose documented purpose is to pair with Factiii cloud/mobile clients over WebRTC and run AI coding agents on the installer's host with shell and subprocess control. dist/cli.js contains onDataChannel/datachannel handlers alongside child_process.spawn and PTY activity, with the control plane fixed at https://api.factiii.com (matching the publisher's homepage). The agent is user-invoked via the `factiii-runner start` bin entry or an opt-in `service install`; there are no npm lifecycle hooks that start it on install. Pairing uses browser OAuth with a JWT, and credentials are stored AES-256-GCM-sealed via the OS keychain with 0600 permissions; the local embedder binds to 127.0.0.1 behind an HMAC bearer. The remote-control capability, blast radius (full shell/PTY on the host), and control-plane host are therefore as advertised rather than covert, and no collateral secret harvesting, credential scraping, or install-time execution was identified. The embedded Python helper and bundled JS use POST/GET and a ping primitive consistent with the documented agent/control flows rather than exfiltration to an unrelated endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
